receipts.first_text_witness: Meet Alan, 32 years old, makes 70 grand a year doing something with spreadsheets that he couldn't explain to you if you asked. He's been investing for 6 years, every paycheck a chunk goes straight into his index funds. He's done everything right, and his account just crossed $48,000. He does the math one night after his third beer and realizes at this rate he'll hit a million dollars right around the time he turns 78. He considers throwing his laptop into the ocean. Here's what Alan doesn't know yet. In exactly 11 years and 4 months something breaks in his account. Not in a bad way, in a way that will permanently change his relationship with money, with time, with work, and with the phrase I can't afford it. He doesn't see it coming. His financial advisor doesn't mention it. No one at his job talks about it. But when it happens Alan will stop being the engine of his own wealth, and something else will quietly take the wheel. That moment is $500,000 invested, and today I'm showing you exactly what happens when you cross it. My name is Nick, and on this channel I break down the math the rest of personal finance YouTube is too scared to actually show you. If that sounds like your kind of thing, do me a quick favor and hit that subscribe button before we get into this, because what I'm about to walk you through is the single most important number most investors will ever hit, and almost nobody explains it honestly. Let's go.
receipts.last_text_witness: work alone. Everything after that gets easier, faster, more automatic. $500,000 looks like a mountain until you're standing on it. Then, you look down and realize most of the climbing happened in the first third of the trip, and the rest was just not quitting. The machine just needs time. Your only job is to keep feeding it and stop trying to help. I'll see you in the next one.
